note: Steps with source 'doc' come straight from the process document and must round-trip against it. Steps with source 'proposed' do not exist in the document yet and need the doc owner's ratification before they are treated as org process.

steps.text: Assign roles for the project
steps.detail: Data Modeler, Data Engineer, Data or Business Analyst, Data Steward or SME, and Stakeholder.

steps.text: Set up design documents from the templates
Request existing artifacts, if any are available
Determine the minimally viable product
steps.detail: Usually one or two Power BI reports demonstrating accurate data and measures with simple visuals. Non-production test reports.

steps.text: Conduct the project kick-off
steps.detail: Define scope around a single business event using the BEAM template, agree the MVP, and estimate level of effort and timeframe (Small 1-2 months, Medium 3-4, Large 6-9).

gate.text: Stakeholder acceptance of project scope and MVP

steps.text: Interview business users and subject matter experts
steps.detail: The BEAM interview outline covers modelstorming, the W questions in order, and grain.

steps.text: Profile the identified source and raw tables
Identify historical data requirements
steps.detail: Which dimensions need slowly changing history, and to what depth.

steps.text: Identify security requirements (CLS and RLS)
Request the source system ERD or data objects, if applicable
Create the conceptual and logical ERD for the target dimensional model
Review and update the data warehouse bus matrix

gate.text: Stakeholder acceptance of the star schema design

steps.text: Review the ETL Standards and Guidelines document
Record the size of each data source
steps.detail: Number of tables, and number of rows per table.

steps.text: Establish connections to the data sources
steps.detail: Skip if reusing existing connections.

steps.text: Determine the data ingestion pattern
steps.detail: Daily snapshots, insert/update, CDC, or streaming.

steps.text: Determine the data refresh rate
steps.detail: Real-time, daily, weekly, or monthly.

steps.text: Develop pipelines or dataflows to extract and load raw data
Apply the stage layer naming convention
steps.detail: Prefix tables with 'zstage', follow source system naming as closely as possible, and use the source system as the schema (workday, virtuous, gapp).

steps.text: Create the stored procedure to insert data into the appropriate data marts
Compare profiled values against business expectations for QA
Create QA tests and validate data types
steps.detail: SSNs, postal codes, phone numbers, numeric values.

steps.text: Enrich the data
steps.detail: Translate IDs, codes, and Booleans into business-readable values.

steps.text: Integrate data across sources, if applicable
Use MDM to merge and resolve duplicate records
Join tables with related attributes into denormalized base tables
Apply the base layer naming convention
steps.detail: Prefix tables with 'base' and use a business term for the schema (HR, Logistics, Finance, Mobi, Advancement, Campaigns).

steps.text: Refer to the BEAM tables and conceptual ERD for the star schema design
Use the bus matrix to identify conforming dimensions
Build dimension tables and add surrogate keys
steps.detail: Use appropriate window functions, for example dense_rank() or identity().

steps.text: Build fact tables from the dimension tables using surrogate keys
Apply the star schema naming convention
steps.detail: Prefix tables with 'fact' or 'dim' and use a business term for the schema.

stages.title: Semantic Model Development in Power BI

steps.text: Create the new Power BI model from the .pbit template
Import the dimensional model tables into the .pbix
Prepare the model per the Power BI Standards document
steps.detail: Mark key columns, create relationships, turn off default aggregations, clean up data formats, create display folders.

steps.text: Create measures and calculation groups
steps.detail: Give each measure a description explaining what it calculates as you go. The check comes later, at AI Readiness; the writing is cheapest now.

steps.text: Run initial tests and improve DAX performance
Review data classification for the fact and dimension tables
Set up security roles for CLS and RLS, and create or update AAD groups
Publish to the testing workspace in the Service

stages.heads_up: Write descriptions as you create tables, columns, and measures. They are not checked until AI Readiness, because demanding them mid-build buries everything else -- but writing 80 of them in one sitting afterwards is the worst way to get them. Data Agent reads the first 200 characters of each one.

stages.title: AI Readiness (Prep for AI)
stages.proposal_note: The process document has no Prep for AI step, so the 20 Data Agent checks have nowhere to attach. This stage is a proposal for the document owner, not ratified org process.

steps.text: Write descriptions for every table, column, and measure
steps.detail: Data Agent reads the first 200 characters of a description to decide what an object is for.

steps.text: Configure Prep for AI > Simplify data schema
steps.detail: Select only the tables, columns, and measures the agent needs. Selecting everything defeats the purpose.

steps.text: Write the AI instructions
steps.detail: Business terminology, fiscal periods, preferred measures per question type, and how to use calculation groups or field parameters.

steps.text: Create verified answers for the most common questions
steps.detail: Five to seven complete trigger questions each, plus up to three filters.

steps.text: Set up the UAT sheet from the template to track bugs and fixes
Verify the accuracy of the data and the measures
Test and improve DAX performance
Test the security roles and access
Create QA checks in Power BI, if applicable
Clean up development and test work
steps.detail: Drop test tables and views, review code formatting.

steps.text: Create stored procedures to automate the build
Add or remove tables in the data catalog and data request app
Develop and deliver user documentation and training
Push the semantic model to the production workspace and grant access
Determine the deployment method for the reports
steps.detail: Workspaces, a Power BI app, an embed link, or export to PDF and Excel.

steps.text: Create wireframes of the MVP reports
Build simple reports with business users and hand off to superusers
Review the work completed against the scope and MVP agreement
Address parking lot items and set priority for the backlog queue
